title: Show Reference Line
content: **Show Reference Line** \- Show or hide Reference Lines to be used when editing Patterns. \- The **Show Reference Line** option is activated by default. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022676787/mceclip0.png) **Edit Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar. Then, select and move a point on the Pattern. The original shape of the Pattern will appear as a Reference Line. If a Pattern does not carry a Reference Line, it will not appear even after selecting **Show Reference Line**. \- To hide the Reference Line, right click on the 2D window and select **Show Reference Line** from the pop-up menu.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to show or hide Reference Lines while editing Patterns in the software, enhancing the editing experience by maintaining visual context.

title: Press
content: **List of Contents** Press Simulate Sewing Line Type **Press** \- Press 3D Garments to flatten bulged Seamlines when more than two layers are sewn together. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649048/mceclip0.png) **Press** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 3D Garment ▶ **Press -**With the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649048/mceclip0.png) **Press** tool selected, navigate to the 3D window and click on the Pattern to be flattened. \- The selected Pattern will disappear. \- Click the other Pattern sewn to the first Pattern. \- The Pattern that was clicked for the first time will appear again. ** Simulate** \- Activate the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649088/mceclip1.png) **Simulation** tool. \- The bulged Seamline will be flattened. ** Sewing Line Type** \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022649048/mceclip0.png)**Press** tool is used to a Pattern, its all Sewing Lines’ Sewing Line Type changed to Turned(ver4.1.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on using the Press tool in CLO 3D to flatten bulged seamlines in 3D garments.

title: Show Mesh
content: **Objective** Show or hide mesh structure that 3D Garments are composed of. Mesh forms are various depending on Patterns, Internal Lines and Sewing state. ** Location** **2D Pattern Window** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern Rendering Style ▶**Mesh** **3D Garment Window** Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 3D Garment Rendering Style ▶**Mesh** 3D Icon ▶ Garment Rendering Style ▶ **Mesh**
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide users with the ability to visualize and toggle the mesh structure of 3D garments, influenced by various patterns, internal lines, and sewing states.

title: Edit Blocks
content: **List of Contents** Edit Patterns Replace Patterns ## Objective Open and edit Patterns in provided Blocks from the Modular Configurator or replace them with your own. Location Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** ## **Operation** **Edit Patterns** 1. Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶ **Block Editor** 3. Select a Block to edit in the list of the Block Editor. → Remaining Blocks are frozen. 4. Modify it with the**![edit_pattern.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026694688/edit_pattern.png) Edit Pattern **tool. 5. Once the modification is done, Simulate the according Block when the rest of the Blocks are still frozen. 6. Once the modification is completed, reselect the selected Block. → All of the Blocks are activated again. **Replace Patterns** 1. Load Blocks from the Modular Configurator. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode ▶**Block Editor** 3. Locate Patterns out of Block Boxes or delete them. → The Block Boxes remain in light grey. 4. Add desired Garment files to substitute with. 5. Click and drag the Patterns that are just loaded to matching Block Boxes. → The Patterns are linked with the Block Boxes. 6. Sew the Patterns to Block Boxes. 7. Select the according Block in the Block Editor, freeze the rest, then **Simulate**. **※ Note: ** * Selected Blocks in the Block Editor are also selected in the 2D window. * Editing Pattern in the Modular Mode is the same as the Simulation Mode. Deleting a segment or a point in a Pattern also deletes Sewing Lines between the Pattern and the Block Box. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for editing and replacing patterns within Blocks using the Modular Configurator's Block Editor.

title: Apply Grading
content: **List of Contents** Apply Grading Apply Existing Size Group Create and Apply Size Group **Apply Grading ** \- Create multiple sizes for Patterns by adding Size Group. \- Apply Existing Size Group Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ ![____17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182548/____17.png)**Assign to Selected Pattern** button next to the Size Group Create and Apply Size Group Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ **Assign To New Rule** **Apply Existing Size Group** \- With the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182068/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png)**Transform Pattern** tool, select Pattern to apply existing Size Group. \- Then, click ![____17.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182548/____17.png)**Assign to Selected** **Pattern** button next to the desired Size Group from the Object Browser. \- Assigned grading appears in pink highlight when the Size Group is selected. **Create and Apply Size Group** \- With the ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001182068/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Transform.png)**Transform Pattern** tool, select Pattern to apply a new Size Group. \- Click **Assign To New Rule** button on the right top of the Object Browser to create and apply a new Size Group to the selected Pattern. ※Note : Grading information will be maintained even after the Patterns are Cut(ver.4.2.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on applying and creating size groups for pattern grading in CLO 3D, including step-by-step instructions and visual aids.

title: Particle Distance Setting
content: ### **Objective** Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. **Location** Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Particle Distance** **Operation** 1. Select Pattern(s). 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Particle Distance ** 3. Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0') 4. Press Enter on keyboard to apply.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting Particle Distance in garment simulation to optimize both quality and speed during the design process.

title: Trace
content: **List of Contents** Trace Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes Trace as an Internal Shape Trace as an Internal Shape vs. Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes Trace as a Pattern Trace with Guidelines **Trace** \- Trace Baselines, Internal Lines and Pattern outlines as Internal Lines and Patterns. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022745867/mceclip0.png) **Trace** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D Pattern ▶ **Trace.** ** Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** * **Select Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern Outlines **\- Click on the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines to be traced. \- Or, click and drag to encompass the desired items into the marquee box. \- The selected items will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace ** \- Right-click on the selected item and choose **Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** or**Trace as an Internal Shape.** **Trace as an Internal Shape** * **Select Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern Outlines ** \- To trace Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines as a shape, all selected lines need to be joined. \- Click on the Baselines, Internal Lines, or Pattern outlines to be traced. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select multiple items. \- Or, click and drag to encompass the desired items into the marquee box. \- The selected items will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace ** \- Right-click on the selected item and choose Trace as **Internal Lines/ Shapes** or **Trace as an Internal Shape.** **Trace as an Internal Shape vs. Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes** * **Trace as an Internal Shape ** \- Use this option extract a closed shape as the shape created by the intersecting lines. \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines that form the desired shape. Then, right-click and select **Trace as an Internal Shape**. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746067/mceclip1.png)**Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and select the shape just traced. \- The closed shape will be highlighted in yellow. * **Trace as Internal Lines/ Shapes ** \- Use this option to trace intersecting lines as individual and separated lines. \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines to be traced. Then, right-click and select **Trace as an Internal Lines/ Shapes.** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022746067/mceclip1.png) **Transform Pattern** tool from the 2D toolbar and select the lines just traced. \- Each traced lines will be selected individually. **Trace as a Pattern** \- Click all items such as Baselines, Internal Lines, and Pattern outlines that form a shape. \- Right-click on the selected items and choose **Trace as Pattern.** \- To trace a shape as a Pattern, all lines’ ends need to be adjoining each other. \- When more than three intersecting lines are selected, a shape formed by them will be traced as a Pattern. **Trace with Guidelines_ver.5.0.0 and Above** \- Select guidelines with Internal Lines or Pattern Outlines, and then right click to select the desired Trace option. \- Make sure to right click on the Internal Line or the Pattern Outline when tracing with guidelines. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on using the Trace tool in the 2D pattern editor to create internal lines, shapes, and patterns effectively.

title: Internal Rectangle Tool
content: ### **Objective** Create a rectangle inside a Pattern. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001039208/________.png) **Internal Rectangle** ** Operation** **Create Internal Rectangle** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001039208/________.png) **Internal Rectangle ** 2. Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an Internal Rectangle. **※ Note:** * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a square (ver.5.1.0). * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a square Internal Shape by its center point (ver.5.1.0). 3. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Rectangle. **Create Internal Rectangle with Measurement Input** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Rectangle ** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001039208/________.png) **Internal Rectangle ** 2. Click once within a Pattern. → The Create Rectangle window appears. 3. Enter appropriate values in the options indicated below. **Width** | Set width of an Internal Rectangle. ---|--- **Height** | Set height of an Internal Rectangle. **![__.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115005595747/__.png) **| Link width and height to adjust them in a fixed ratio. **Position** | **Outline** | Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the outline of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0). **Center** | Set left, right, top and bottom position of an internal rectangle on the basis of the center of the Internal Rectangle (ver2.5.0).
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating an internal rectangle within a 2D pattern using the Clo3D software, including options for freehand drawing and precise measurement input.

title: Distribute
content: **Objective** Distribute Patterns or/and Internal Shapes/Lines by designated intervals (ver2.5.0). ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶**Horizontally** /**Vertically** ** Operation** 1. Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001010987/1.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001011007/2.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Select two or more Patterns or/and Internal Lines/Shapes. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern/Internal Line/Shape) ▶ Distribute ▶ **Horizontally** /**Vertically** →The Distribute Window appears. 4. Enter the desired Spacing value and select **OK**. →The selected Patterns and/or Internal Lines/Shapes are distributed horizontally or vertically by the designated intervals.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for users to easily distribute patterns and internal shapes or lines at specified intervals using the right-click pop-up menu in the 2D toolbar.

title: 2D Snapshot
content: **List of Contents** 2D Snapshot Apply 2D Snapshot Save 2D Snapshot **2D Snapshot** \- Save Patterns in 1:1 ratio as images. \- Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **2D Patterns(1:1).** **Apply 2D Snapshot** \- The 2D window expands and the 2D Snapshot window appears. * **Size**** ** * Preset Select one among provided Presets. * Orientation Decide orientation of the image. * Width, Height Type in desired Width and Height for the image. * Resolution Assign Resolution for the image. * **Option**** ** * Select which lines will be included in the exported image. * Select which images will be included in the exported image. * Select additional information included in the exported image. * Save the image with transparent background. **Save 2D Snapshot** * **Save as .****Png ** * Configure all options, click Save, and select the Save as Type as .png. * **Save as .****Pdf ** * Configure all options, click Save, and select the Save as Type as .pdf. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides users with tools and options to apply and save 2D patterns as images in various formats, allowing for customizable snapshots with specified dimensions and settings.

title: Freeze
content: **List of Contents** Freeze Result of Freeze Features of Freeze **Freeze** \- Freeze selected Patterns to fix them like a hardware. \- Select desired Patterns to be frozen and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select **Freeze.** ** Result of Freeze** \- When the selected Patterns are frozen, the Patterns will turn light-blue. When the Simulation is activated, Patterns be fixed in the 3D environment. \- To unfreeze the selected Patterns, right click again and select **Unfreeze.** **Features of Freeze** \- Frozen Patterns will be calculated for collision because they are considered as hard objects like Avatars. \- Therefore, activated Patterns cannot freely pass through the frozen Patterns. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to freeze selected patterns for simulation, detailing the process, results, and features of the freeze function.

title: Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing)
content: **List of Contents** Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) Result of Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) Features of Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) **Deactivate (Pattern& Sewing)** \- Deactivate selected Patterns and their Sewing lines to easily perform meticulous editing on the 3D Garment. \- Select desired Patterns to be deactivated and right click to access the pop-up menu. Then, select Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing). ** Result of Deactivate (Pattern& Sewing)** \- When the selected Patterns and Sewing Lines are properly deactivated, Patterns should turn translucent navy while the Sewing Lines turn white. Even when the Simulation is activated, deactivated Patterns and Sewing Lines will not move and activated Patterns will not be sewn to the deactivated Patterns. \- To activate the selected Patterns and Sewing Lines, right click again and select **Activate.** **Features of Deactivate (Pattern& Sewing)** \- Deactivated Patterns will not be calculated for collision. \- Simulate overlapped Patterns, one being activated and the other being deactivated. The activated Pattern will easily pass through the deactivated Pattern. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive overview of the Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing) feature, allowing users to selectively deactivate patterns and sewing lines for precise 3D garment editing.

title: 2D Pattern (PACX) Open/Add/Save
content: **Objective** Save 2D Patterns as *.pacx file format. This format can only be saved or reopened and edited in CLO. ** Location** **Open Pattern** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Pattern ****Add Pattern ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ **Pattern ****Save Pattern ** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Pattern** ** Operation** **Open Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ **Pattern** → The Open File window is opened. 2. Select the desired file and click the **Open** button. **Add Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶**Pattern** → The Add Pattern window is opened 2. Select the file to add and click the **Open** button to add the Pattern file. **Save Pattern** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ **Pattern** → The Save File window is opened. 2. Select a location to save the Pattern file to, type in a name and press the **Save** button. → A *.pacx file is created.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on saving, opening, and adding 2D patterns in the *.pacx file format exclusively for use in CLO.

title: Replace as Pattern Outline
content: ### **Objective** Substitute Pattern outlines with Internal Lines, establishing the Internal Line as the new Pattern outline. ### **Location** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008329508/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** ### **Operation** 1. [Create an internal line](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000481707) to be substituted with the Pattern outline. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ ![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115008329508/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png) **Edit Pattern** 3. Click on the Internal Line and the Pattern outline that should be replaced. → The Internal Line and Pattern outline are highlighted in yellow. 4. Right-click on the selected Internal Line or Pattern outline. → A pop-up menu appears. 5. Select the**Replace as Pattern Outline** option. → The selected Pattern outline is replaced with the shape of the Internal Line. → The original Pattern outline appears as a Reference Line.
content_description: This page provides a step-by-step guide for substituting Pattern outlines with Internal Lines in the 2D Toolbar, enhancing your pattern editing workflow.

title: Edit Annotation
content: **List of Contents** Edit Annotation Move Delete **Edit Annotation ** \- Move or delete annotations on 2D Patterns. \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![edit_annotation.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001215807/edit_annotation.png)**Edit Annotation** **Move** ** ** \- Click and drag the annotation to be moved. **Delete** **** \- Click on the annotation to be deleted. \- Right-click to access the right-click pop-up menu. \- Select **Delete** option. \- Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides instructions for editing, moving, and deleting annotations on 2D patterns within the software.

title: Import - DXF
content: **List of Contents** Import DXF Import (Add) DXF **Import DXF** \- CLO is compatible with most of Pattern CAD such as YUKA, Gerber, Lectra, StyleCAD, Optitex, and PAD System in DXF-AAMA and DXF-ASTM file formats. \- Import 2D Patterns to use in CLO. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import ▶ **DXF (AAMA/ASTM). ** \- Locate the DXF file and select **Open.** \- The Import DXF window will appear. \- **Load Type** : Select either to open or add the DXF file. \- **Scale** : select the unit used to create the Patterns. When the **Auto Scale** option is selected, CLO will detect the unit of the Patterns automatically. \- **Rotation** : select the direction that the Patterns will be rotated to. -**Option** : Check following options as needed: Import Pattern Annotation, Auto-Trace as Internal Lines, Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line, Auto Distribute, and Optimize All Curve Points. \- Select OK to open the Patterns based on the settings. ** Import (Add) DXF** \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ **DXF (AAMA/ASTM). ** \- Locate the DXF file and select **Open.** \- The selected DXF file will be added to the workspace. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on importing DXF files into CLO, detailing the necessary steps and options for seamless integration of 2D patterns from various Pattern CAD systems.

title: Edit Line (3D Pattern)
content: **List of Contents** Edit Line (3D Pattern) Edit 3D Line Delete 3D Line Right Click Pop-Up Menu on 3D Line **Edit Line (3D Pattern)** \- Select, delete and Edit 3D lines created on draped Garments in the 3D Window. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021985308/mceclip0.png) **Edit line (3D Line)** tool from the 3D toolbar. ** Edit 3D Line** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021985308/mceclip0.png) **Edit Line (3D Line)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click and drag the point on the 3D Line to make adjustments. **Delete 3D Line** \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021985308/mceclip0.png) **Edit Line (3D Line)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Click on the 3D Line, then hit the Delete key or the Backspace key on the keyboard to delete. **Right Click Pop-up Menu on 3D Line** \- Right-click on the 3D Line to access the pop-up menu and select options as below for desired actions. * **Delete** \- The selected 3D Line will be deleted. * **Cut** \- Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- When a 3D Line is drawn only on one of the symmetric Patterns, only the Pattern with the 3D Line will be cut and the linked editing function will be removed. * **Cut & Sew** \- Cut and Sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- When a 3D Line is drawn only on one of the symmetric Patterns, only the Pattern with the 3D Line will be cut and sewn and the linked editing function will be removed. * **(Symmetry) Cut** \- Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- Even if the selected 3D Line is drawn on only one of the Symmetric Patterns, both Symmetric Patterns will be cut and linked editing function will be maintained. * **(Symmetry) Cut & Sew** \- Cut and Sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Line. \- Even if the selected 3D Line is drawn on only one of the Symmetric Patterns, both Symmetric Patterns will be cut and sewn and linked editing function will be maintained. * **Trace as Internal Shape** \- Trace the selected 3D Line as an Internal Shape. * **Convert to Internal Shape** \- Convert the selected 3D Lines to an Internal Shape. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to edit, delete, and utilize 3D lines in garment design within the 3D window, including detailed instructions for various tools and right-click menu options.

title: Edit 3D Pen (Garment) Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
content: ### **Objective** Edit desired 3D Pen lines using the right-click pop-up menu. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ ![Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000022028/Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png) **Edit 3D Pen (Garment)** ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶**![Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000022028/Edit_Line__3D_Pattern_.png) Edit 3D Pen (Garment) ** 2. Right click on the desired 3D Pen line. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Refer to below table and select an appropriate option. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Delete** | Delete the selected 3D Pen line. **Add Point** | Add a Segment Point to the selected 3D Pen line. **Add Curve Point** | Add a Curve Point to the selected 3D Pen line. **Cut** | Cut the Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. **Cut & Sew** | Cut and sew the Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. **Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern (ver5.0.0)** | Duplicate the selected 3D Pen line to its [Symmetric Pattern](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000354528-%EB%8F%99%EC%8B%9C-%EC%88%98%EC%A0%95-%ED%8C%A8%ED%84%B4-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95). **Symmetric** | **Cut** | Cut the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. **Cut & Sew** | Cut and sew the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern based on the selected 3D Pen line. **Trace as Internal Shape** | Trace the selected 3D Pen line as Internal Shapes on the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern. **Convert to Internal Shape** | Convert the selected 3D Pen line as Internal Shapes on the Pattern and its Symmetric Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides instructions on how to edit 3D Pen lines in a garment design using the right-click pop-up menu in the 3D Toolbar.

title: Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline
content: **List of Contents** Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline Use Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline **Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline** \- Extend or trim the Internal Line to Pattern outline. \- Right-click on the Internal Line and select **Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline** from the pop-up menu. ** Use Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline** \- Use the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022471348/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022402107/mceclip1.png) **Edit Pattern** tool to right click on the Internal Line \- Select **Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline** from the pop-up menu. \- The selected Internal Line will extend or trim to the Pattern outline. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to use the "Extend/Trim to Pattern Outline" feature in CLO 3D for modifying internal lines to match the pattern outline.

title: Edit Grading Properties
content: **List of Contents** Grading Properties Select Pattern with Grading Edit Grading Properties **Grading Properties** ** ** \- Edit grading rules applied to the selected Pattern. \- Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Grading** \- 2D Toolbar ▶ ![grading.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360001205408/grading.png)**Grading** **Select Pattern with Grading** ** ** \- Click on the Pattern outline or point which its grading rule to be edited. \- Selected Pattern outline or point’s grading properties appear in the Property Editor. \- If there is no applied grading rule on the selected Pattern outline or point, an error message appears alerting “No graded size available to edit. **Edit Grading Properties** **** * **Distance** Edit selected Pattern outline or point’s grading rules. Use the Distance option to assign each Size’s distance apart from its Base Size. * Size All Sizes belong to the applied Size Group appear. X-Axis Shift the Size on X-axis. Y-Axis Shift the Size on Y-axis. * **Offset** Edit selected Pattern outline or point’s grading rules. Use the Offset option to edit distance between each size. * Size All Sizes belong to the applied Size Group appear. X-Axis Shift the Size on X-axis. Y-Axis Shift the Size on Y-axis. All Edit all Offset values at once(ver4.1.0). * **Arrow Key Movement** Assign the distance to be moved when using arrow keys. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for managing and editing grading properties in 2D patterns, including selecting patterns, adjusting grading rules, and utilizing offset options for precise size adjustments.

title: Duplicate as Mirrored Internal Line
content: ### **Objective** Mirror paste Pattern Outline or Internal Line to compare with original Pattern Outlines before the edit. ** Location** Right Click (On Pattern Outline or Internal Line) ▶ **Duplicate as Mirrored Internal Line** ** Operation** 1. Select the **![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360019459094/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Follow the path indicated below: Right Click (On Pattern Outline or Internal Line) ▶ **Duplicate as Mirrored Internal Line **** →** A guide appears for you to select a reference line which the selected Pattern Outline or the Internal Line to be mirror based accordingly. 3. Hover the mouse over the reference line. → The reference line turns light blue. → A preview appears where the mirrored Pattern Outline or Internal Line will be duplicated to. 4. Select the desired reference line. → The Pattern Outline or the Internal Line is duplicated based on the selected reference line. → The duplicated Internal Line belongs to the Pattern selected in step 2.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to duplicate a Pattern Outline or Internal Line as a mirrored Internal Line for comparison with the original before editing.

title: Create Buttons along Pattern Outline
content: **List of Contents** Create Select Unlink ### **Objective** Create buttons along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance.. **Location ** Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ **Button** 3D toolbar ▶ **Button** ** Operation** **Create** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click on the outline or internal line of the pattern. → The button/buttonhole creation option window appears along the pattern outline. **※Note:** Hold down the Shift key and left-click on a segment to select multiple. 3. Set each option and click OK. **Type**** ** | Start Position | Repeatedly create a button based on the starting point. ---|---|--- Distribute | Create by aligning buttons at regular intervals between the starting and ending points. **Based on Start**** ** | **Start Position** | Distance | Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and the center of the button. Interval | Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the button. Reverse | The starting point of the button and replicated created direction are adjusted in reverse. **Replicate** | Interval | Adjust the distance between the buttons. Number of Buttons/Buttonholes | Adjust the number of buttons. **Distribute** | **Position** | Distance | Adjust the distance between the clicked segment and t he center of the button. Start/End Interval | Adjust the spacing between the pattern outline and the center of the start/end buttons. **Replicate** | Number of Buttons/Buttonholes | Enter the number of buttons/buttonholes to align between the start and end points. → A group button is created. **Select** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Click a button or segment created along the pattern outline. → All grouped buttons are selected. 3. Change the [button properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115005617768--Property-Button-Property-Setting-) and [style](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/sections/115000728968-%EB%8B%A8%EC%B6%94-%EC%8A%A4%ED%83%80%EC%9D%BC-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) or [right-click](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115002227747--Popup-Button-Right-Click-Menus). → Applied to grouped buttons. → Group information is not copied/pasted. **※Note:** * If clicking again on the selected group button, it is able to select a button individually. * Grouped buttons cannot be moved. **Unlink** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location.** ** 2. After right-clicking on a button or segment created along the pattern outline and click **Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes**. **** → The group is unlinked.** **
content_description: This web page provides a detailed guide on creating, selecting, and unlinking buttons along a pattern outline in a 3D design tool, ensuring precise placement and customization.

title: Internal Ellipse
content: **List of Contents** Create Internal Ellipse Create Internal Ellipse with Entered Values ### **Objective** Create internal ellipses or circles within Patterns. **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Ellipse** ** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115002222408/_______.png) **Internal Ellipse** **Operation** **Create Internal Ellipse** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Ellipse**** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115002222408/_______.png) **Internal Ellipse** 2. Click and drag within a Pattern to freehand an ellipse. Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to create a circle. **※ Note:** * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to create it by the center point (ver.5.1.0). * While creating the Internal Shape, press down the Shift + Ctrl keys to create a full circle by its center point (ver.5.1.0). 3. Release the mouse to complete the Internal Ellipse or the Internal Circle. **Create Internal Ellipse with Entered Values** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Create ▶ **Internal Ellipse**** **2D Toolbar ▶![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115002222408/_______.png) **Internal Ellipse** 2. Click once within a Pattern. → The Create Ellipse window appears. 3. Enter the desired values. **Diameter** | Set the diameter of the Internal Circle. ---|--- **Radius** | Set the radius of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). **![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360054822354/mceclip0.png)**| Link to maintain the width and height ratio. **Circumference** | Set the circumference of the Internal Circle (ver3.2.0). **Position** | **To Outline** | Set the position of the left, right, top, and bottom of the Internal Circles from the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). **To Center** | Set the position of the center of the Internal Circle from the left, right, top, and bottom of the Pattern outline (ver2.5.0). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on how to create internal ellipses or circles within patterns using the 2D Pattern tools in Clo3D.

title: Preview and Select AI Artboards
content: **List of Contents** Preview and Select AI Artboards Add Graphic **Preview and Select AI Artboards ** \- When the AI file imported as a graphic has multiple artboards, preview and select the one in need. \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select Materials ▶ Graphics ▶ **Graphic (2D/3D) ** \- Or, select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026562207/mceclip0.png) **Graphic (2D/ 3D)** tool from the 2D or 3D toolbar. ** Add Graphic** * **3D Window** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026562207/mceclip0.png) **Graphic (3D Pattern)** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Choose the AI file to be imported. \- When the selected AI file has multiple artboards, the Preview window appears allowing you to select the desired artboard. \- After the artboard is selected, the Add Graphic window appears, allowing you to adjust the graphic size. * **Width** \- Set the width of the graphic. * **Height** \- Set the height of the graphic. \- Click OK to complete. * **2D Window** \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115026562207/mceclip0.png) **Graphic (2D Pattern)** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Choose the AI file to be imported. \- When the selected AI file has multiple artboards, the Preview window appears allowing you to select the desired artboard. \- After the artboard is selected, the Add Graphic window appears, allowing you to adjust the graphic size. * **Width** \- Set the width of the graphic. * **Height** \- Set the height of the graphic. * **Outline** \- Locate the graphic by assigning the margin between the Pattern outline and the graphic outline. * **Center** \- Locate the graphic by assigning the distance between the Pattern outline and the center of the graphic. \- Click OK to complete. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for previewing and selecting AI artboards to add graphics in both 2D and 3D environments.

title: Copy/Paste Patterns (3D)
content: **Objective** Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window. ## ** **Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ **Copy** or **Paste** ## ** **Operation 1. Select the ![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024515248/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ **Copy** or **Paste** → A preview of the copied pattern follows the mouse cursor. 3. Click on the desired location in the 3D window to place the duplicated pattern. → The copied pattern is automatically assigned a number. **※ Note:** * To copy and paste more efficiently, select the pattern, press Ctrl+C, then press Ctrl+V or Ctrl+R on the keyboard to copy, paste or mirror paste, respectively. * Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window to another CLO software window (ver3.0.0). This is only available in Windows. * Trims and buttons are also copied and pasted along with Patterns (ver5.0.0.) * In the case of buttons and/or subsidiary materials in the pattern, they cannot be copied and pasted into other programs.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to efficiently copy and paste patterns within the 3D window of CLO software, enabling users to enhance their design workflow.

title: Perpendicular Pattern Corner (ver 6.1)
content: ### **Objective** Adjust pattern corners to be perpendicular in curved patterns such as armholes and the center front rise of the pants. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ **Edit Pattern** ** **2D Toolbar▶![Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360000037167/Toolbar_2D_Pattern_Edit.png)**Edit Pattern** ** Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. 2. Right-click the point of the corner to be set as perpendicular then select **Perpendicular Pattern Corner** from the right-click menu. → The pop-up window appears. 3. After setting the options, click the OK Button. Length | Input the length of the segment to be perpendicular to the opposite segment. ---|--- Direction | Set the direction as perpendicular. **** **※ Note:** The number of curve points can be increased to maintain the curvature of the original pattern. At this time, [optimize the number of curve points](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000527527-%EA%B3%A1%EC%84%A0%EC%A0%90-%EC%B5%9C%EC%A0%81%ED%99%94) as needed.
content_description: Learn how to adjust pattern corners to achieve perpendicular angles in curved designs for enhanced garment fitting and aesthetics.

title: Copy/Duplicate Graphic Image
content: **List of Contents** Copy/Paste Graphic Image Duplicate Graphic Image ### **Objective** Copy/paste or duplicate graphic images as needed. **Location** Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu ▶ **Copy**(Ctrl + C), **Paste**(Ctrl + V) / **Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern** **Operation** **Copy/Paste Graphic Image** 1. Select a graphic image with ![____156.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115019288628/____156.png) **Edit Texture** tool or ![____156-1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115019199047/____156-1.png) **Transform Graphic** tool in the 2D window. 2. content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for copying and duplicating graphic images in the 2D window using the right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu.

title: 2D Pattern - Exporting Patterns from Gerber(Gerber Pattern Design)
content: **Objective ** Export patterns as a DXF file from Gerber in order to use them in CLO. ** Operation** 1. Load the pattern to be exported, and click File ▶ **Export**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768368/72.png) 2. Click on the patterns to be exported. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768348/69.png) 3. Upon clicking the pattern, the Export window will open up, as shown below. Set the File Type to Amma (*.dxf) and press the **Options** button on the bottom. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005715787/70.png) 4. Check all the sections and press **OK**. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768308/71__1_.png) 5. When a window like the one shown below appears, press **OK** to continue. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768368/72.png) 6. Ensure that there are no irregularities in the exported pattern, and press **Close** to complete the export. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005768388/73..png)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to exporting patterns as DXF files from Gerber for use in CLO.

title: Layer Clone
content: **Objective** Create an instance of the Pattern in its 3D state while sewing its Pattern outlines and Internal Lines to its instance's Pattern outlines and Internal Lines. Use the function to easily create padded jackets, collars, cuffs and other garments/details made with multiple layers of Patterns. ** Location** Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Layer Clone (Over/Under)** ** Operation** 1. Select ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001062748/1.png) **Transform Pattern** tool or ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115001062728/2.png) **Edit Pattern** tool. 2. Select the Patterns to be layer cloned. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Layer Clone (Over)** → The cloned Pattern is placed above the original Pattern. Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ **Layer Clone (Under)** → The cloned Pattern is placed beneath the original Pattern. 4. Activate **Simulation**. → The cloned layer is simulated based on the option selected.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for utilizing the Layer Clone function in 3D pattern design, enabling users to create multi-layered garments such as padded jackets and collars with ease.

title: Add Perpendicular Internal Lines
content: **List of Contents** Add Perpendicular Internal Lines Add From a Point Add From a Line **Add Perpendicular Internal Lines** \- Create Internal Lines perpendicular to selected Pattern outline or point, or perpendicular to X or Y axis of 2D window. \- Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Right click on the point where an Internal Line should be added and select**Add Perpendicular Internal Line**. ** Add From a Point** * **X-Axis ** \- The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. \- Configure Angle and Length of the Internal Line based on the X axis \- To extend the Internal Line to the Pattern outline, please toggle on **Extend** option. **※****Note:** To add the Internal Line opposite from current direction, toggle on **Reverse** option. * **Y-Axis ** \- The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. \- Configure Angle and Length of the Internal Line based on the Y axis. \- To extend the Internal Line to the Pattern outline, please toggle on **Extend** option. **※****Note:** To add the Internal Line opposite from current direction, toggle on **Reverse** option. * **Local ** \- The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. \- Configure Angle and Length of the Internal Line based on the selected point. \- To extend the Internal Line to the Pattern outline, please toggle on **Extend** option. \- To add the Internal Line based on the opposite side of the selected point, toggle on **Refer to Opposite Segment**. **※****Note:** To add the Internal Line opposite from current direction, toggle on **Reverse** option. **Add From a Line** * **X-Axis ** \- The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. \- Configure Angle and Length of the Internal Line based on the X axis and its Distance to Segment Edge. \- To extend the Internal Line to the Pattern outline, please toggle on **Extend** option. \- When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. **※****Note:** To add the Internal Line opposite from current direction, toggle on **Reverse** option. * **Y-Axis ** \- The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. \- Configure Angle and Length of the Internal Line based on the Y axis and its Distance to Segment Edge. \- To extend the Internal Line to the Pattern outline, please toggle on **Extend** option. \- When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. **※****Note:** To add the Internal Line opposite from current direction, toggle on **Reverse** option. * **Local ** \- The Add Perpendicular Internal Line window appears. \- Configure Angle and Length of the Internal Line based on the selected segment and its Distance to Segment Edge. \- To extend the Internal Line to the Pattern outline, please toggle on**Extend** option. \- When the Length value is different from the length when it is extended, the option turns off automatically. **※****Note:** To add the Internal Line opposite from current direction, toggle on **Reverse** option. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for adding perpendicular internal lines in a 2D design environment, specifically detailing methods for adding lines from points and lines along the X and Y axes.
